subject: URGENT: Pathway Health - sudden 429/timeout surge impacting ingest pipelines
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@pathwayhealth.com>

Subject: Sudden 429/timeout surge - urgent

Hi Aisha,

We're seeing a large spike in 429 responses starting ~08:50 PT from the Redwood API for our ingest pipeline. This is affecting three downstream services and causing cascading timeouts and retries on our side — we're seeing ~6% of calls fail with 429 and a handful of 504 timeouts.

Quick details:
- Primary key: org_id=pathway-prod, project=ingest-main, api_key last 4 = a1b2
- Spike started ~08:50, peaked ~09:05, value-series attached (ingest-qps-timeseries.png).
- Impact: delayed nightly processing, incident page open with our SRE.

We urgently need: confirmation this is on your side, root cause hypothesis, and immediate mitigation (we can temporarily throttle/retry differently if you recommend). I'll upload sample request ids and a partial log export (sent separately).

Rajiv
Pathway Health

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

On Fri, Feb 27, 2027 at 09:27 AM aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Markus/irene — can you prioritize a routing/quota check for the org_id/project above?

Quick findings from initial look:
- We see a burst where requests from project label ingest-main were routed to project-level quota bucket "ingest-main-staging" (low-tier) instead of the customer's reserved project bucket.
- Cause: recent project-label rename during Pathway's infra deploy combined with a stale alias in our tiering-service lookup table. The alias resolved to the wrong project id for ~15m (08:49–09:04).
- Symptoms match: elevated 429s and client retry storms because retries were hitting the same low quota bucket.

Immediate remediation taken (10:02):
- Corrected the alias entry, rerouted live traffic to the reserved project bucket.
- Applied a temporary quota bump for the project to absorb the backlog for 1 hour.

Next steps I recommend:
- Root cause ticket (INF-6123) created to add guardrails for alias churn and add alerting on alias-to-project mismatch.
- Ops: fine-tune the automatic retry backoff guidance for clients to avoid intensified retry storms in the short window.

I've attached a short sample of correlated logs and the timeseries screenshot. Will follow up with a fuller postmortem.

—Markus
Senior SRE, Runtime

Team — looping in sales leadership and ops for an exec-facing summary.

Summary (so we can brief account team + execs quickly):
- Incident: 429 spike + timeouts for Pathway ingest observed 08:50–09:04 PT; elevated retries caused additional pressure.
- Root cause (prelim): project-label rename + stale alias in tiering-service caused routing to low-tier project/quota bucket.
- Mitigation: alias corrected and temporary quota bump applied at 10:02 PT. Nightly backlog is catching up; no data deletion observed, only processing delay.
- Impact: delayed nightly jobs; client reports ~6% request failure rate during window.

Asks / proposed next steps:
1) Support: Offer Pathway 2 weeks' invoice credit and a follow-up SLO review. (Jonas — need approval to propose credit.)
2) Engineering: Complete INF-6123 postmortem with timelines and preventive alerts (Markus/irene).
3) Product/Docs: Publish guidance for project-label changes (best practice for safe label rotations).
4) Customer ops: Confirm final impact metrics and provide an official incident note to Pathway (Aisha to coordinate).

Attachments: sla-evidence-202702.pdf (customer topology + impact), ingest-qps-timeseries.png.

Rajiv, we'll send a formal incident note by EOD and propose the credit amount once we confirm impact.

—Aisha
